summary: St. Joe NF 20-foot pole L-4 lookout in Shoshone County, built 1936; burned in winter 1964-65 and left as ruins, with a conflicting 1967 staff entry.

facts.status_note: Burned in the winter of 1964-65 and left as ruins, per firelookout.com; the Idaho Fire Lookouts site also lists it in ruins

access.note: On St. Joe National Forest land; the Idaho Fire Lookouts site labels the ruins drive-up

visit.trail_note: A 1959 USGS station description of the peak says to pack up a trail about 3 miles from the end of truck travel; the sources disagree on access

events.note: 20-foot pole tower with L-4 cab, as dated on the Forest Lookouts site citing Kresek; firelookout.com and the Idaho site agree on 1936; a log cabin stood about a quarter mile north
Ragnar Benson listed as known lookout personnel
Burned in the winter of 1964-65 per firelookout.com; the 1967 staff entry on the Idaho site does not fit this date
Sherman Rouse listed as known staff, citing Kellogg Evening News

evidence.supports: 1936 20-foot pole L-4 tower, log cabin 1/4 mile north, burned winter 1964/1965, ruins, 1960 Ragnar Benson
evidence.quote: 1936: 20' pole L-4 tower. Log cabin 1/4 mile north. Burned winter 1964/1965. Ruins. Known lookout personnel: 1960: Ragnar Benson.

evidence.supports: 1936 20-foot pole tower with L-4 cab, citing Kresek
1959 USGS station description of the peak
pack up a trail for about 3 miles to the top
evidence.quote: PACK UP TRAIL FOR ABOUT 3 MI. TO TOP AND STATION.

corrections.why: Both sources describe ruins on the site after the 1964-65 burn, so the structure is not wholly gone

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Idaho site labels the ruins drive-up; the 1959 USGS station description says to pack about 3 miles up a trail from the end of truck travel. Both are recorded and current access is not confirmed.
Firelookout.com dates the burn to winter 1964-65, but the Idaho site lists Sherman Rouse as staff in 1967. Both are kept; the sources do not settle which is right.

notes_for_editor: Two open conflicts: the burn date (winter 1964-65) against a 1967 staff entry, and drive-up ruins against a 1959 trail description. Both are left open in the story. Status corrected from gone to ruins because both sources describe standing ruins. No current access rules found.
